# IDEAS MATRIX — every idea explored, with pros, cons and a verdict
### generated by `ideas_matrix.py` from `data/ideas_matrix.json` — edit the JSON, then re-run

> Every idea explored for the Earth House-Kit, with pros, cons and a verdict.
> Verdicts: **WINNER** = in the lead design · adopt = a supporting part of the kit · test = promising, waiting on a measurement · fallback = proven backup · niche = only for certain sites or uses · ~~killed~~ = failed its numbers (the reasons are in `GRAVEYARD.md`).

**13 winner · 12 adopt · 11 test · 7 fallback · 7 niche · 30 killed** — 80 ideas in all.

## The winner design, in one breath
Malvern clay extruded into **cellular units with staggered webs** (graded skin, husk-pored core, dense
ground bed faces), fired in a **husk-gasifier kiln**, dry-stacked into **rod-clamped panels** and tilted up
into a **16–20-sided round plan** locked by **wedged key blocks**, capped by a **post-tensioned ribbed dome**
under **cocciopesto and fired scale tiles**, wearing **hung interlocking siding** and standing on **fluted
drainage boots**. Inside: **bio-lime block partitions** between treated bamboo posts. First product: the
**round drum storm shelter**. Larger homes are **clusters of domes**. Made in a **small Malvern factory**
that ships kits by truckload. Layer-by-layer detail and sources: `SYNTHESIS.md`.

## Making rock

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fire site clay into small units (~1,000 °C)** | 0.9–3.0 MJ/kg from farm waste; 36–46 MPa typical brick; a century of Malvern practice; doesn't rot, burn or rust | needs a kiln and fuel; 5–8% total shrinkage; each clay bed must be tested | **WINNER** | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md, rock_options.py` |
| Geopolymer (soil + fired clay + activator) | actually uses the clay; no cement | 0.3–0.7 t caustic activator per house; ~665 kg panels; handling hazards | test | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |
| Compacted earth tilt-up panels (the original project) | no firing; tilt-up lift checks out (3.0–5.7× with rebar) | not rock: 0.3–1 MPa; 6 in + steel; ~900 kg panels; 7–28 day cure | fallback | `earth-panel/SPEC.md, tiltup_check.py` |
| Solid fired brick laid on site | the proven method everyone trusts | 7.5 in walls, 16–18 t; slow wet trade; mortar | fallback | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |
| Concrete from screened sand and gravel | the known benchmark; 1–3 day lift | 1.1–1.5 t cement per house; fails on clay fines (1.5–3.4 MPa) | niche | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |
| Lime-sand steam-cured blocks | 12–48 h cure; proven industrially | sandy sites only; 1.1–2.0 t lime; heavy 6.5 in walls | niche | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |
| Bio-cemented sandstone (MICP/EICP) | room-temperature 'grown' stone | sand only; ~1 kg ammonium chloride waste per kg calcite; 2–6 t reagents per house | niche | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Melt the soil into rock (vitrification, cast basalt, microwave) | superb stone (cast basalt ≥300 MPa) | 6–12 MWh per house; ~3.5 MW power; big melts cool for 1–2 years | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Fire the whole house in place (Geltaftan) | no assembly; monolithic | tried in Iran and abandoned: fuel cost, pollution, uneven firing | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Fire the whole wall, or only its binder, in place | no kiln to ship | ~12,600 kWh per house; heats a whole wall to fire 15% of it; shrinkage cracking | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Sulfur concrete walls | sets in hours; no water | melts at 115–120 °C and burns to SO₂; can't take swelling clay | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md (maybe plinths, tanks, drains)` |
| Single-piece fired ceramic wall panel | 3 in wall, no joints, no steel | thick site-clay slabs very likely crack in a field kiln; industry only does 6–20 mm pressed slabs | ~~killed~~ | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |

## Units & bricks

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cellular unit: staggered 6-row webs, husk-filled** | U 0.62 and 9 h lag at 8 in; 6–8 mm webs dry in hours; ~32–40% clay | thin webs must survive handling and grinding; impact untested | **WINNER** | `making-system/BRICK_PANEL.md, thermal_check.py` |
| **Extrude the bulk through a die** | fast, uniform, the brick industry's method; one die for all dome voussoirs | a die per cross-section; fixed shapes | **WINNER** | `SYNTHESIS.md, production_line.py` |
| **Grind bed faces flat after firing** | ±0.5 mm, ≤0.2 mm flat makes mortarless work (Poroton Dryfix) | a grinder station and dust control | **WINNER** | `SYNTHESIS.md` |
| 3D-print clay units (bead-built ribs) | any shape; less clay; custom corners, keys and one-offs | slow; warping and layer-line cracking unknown | test | `printer/, making-system/BRICK_PANEL.md` |
| Graded units: glass-cullet skin, husk-pored core, dense rims | 8 in U ≈ 0.42; engobes cut absorption 14.8% → 3.2%; bone-like logic | zones must shrink together; co-extrusion not yet tried | test | `making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Straight-through, diamond or truss web patterns | simpler dies | each web is a heat highway: U 0.76–1.75 | ~~killed~~ | `thermal_check.py` |
| Husk ash as a flux for a glassy skin | free, on site | 90–97% silica: refractory at 1,000 °C and makes cristobalite | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Salt-glazed units | classic waterproof face | needs 1,250–1,300 °C; releases HCl | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Walls & panels

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Dry-stacked panels clamped by 2 rods, tilted up** | ~282–413 kg panels; no cure wait; rods carry 11.7–18.8× the lift if joints open; demountable | joints must stay tight (20–35% prestress loss assumed); untested at full size | **WINNER** | `making-system/BRICK_PANEL.md, brick_panel_check.py` |
| Openings as module-wide gaps with sill and lintel panels | never cut a panel; short lintels (Inca logic) | window sizes follow the module | adopt | `tiltup_check.py` |
| Grouted panels with bars | stronger; the proven path for storm walls | 5–28 day cure; not demountable | fallback | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md, business/SHELTER_PLAN.md` |
| On-site brick building (laying units by hand) | no hoist; familiar | slower than panels; more site labour | fallback | `rock/ROCK_OPTIONS.md` |
| Carbon steel set tight in the masonry | cheap | rust expands and splits it (the Acropolis's 20th-century repairs) | ~~killed~~ | `SYNTHESIS.md §3` |

## Joints & interlocks

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Japanese joinery rules: clay only presses; wedges and rods lock** | no mortar, no glue; every joint re-driven or opened | precision required; steel wedges and rods still bought | **WINNER** | `making-system/KIT_OF_PARTS.md` |
| Wedged fired key blocks at the polygon folds (shachi-sen) | draws panels together with spare travel to re-drive | untested | test | `data/joints.json` |
| Keystone ring: slide in from outside, hook the notch below, lock to a neighbour, pinned key last | can't be pushed through; one assembly order; last piece is the lock | every unit numbered; one broken unit holds up the course | test | `business/SHELTER_PLAN.md, data/joints.json` |
| Clay hooks or tabs that carry tension | no steel | fired clay is weak in tension; Greek masons used separate cramps for this reason | ~~killed~~ | `making-system/KIT_OF_PARTS.md` |
| Guastavino/timbrel 'no formwork' vaulting | famous and fast | works only because gypsum glues each tile; dry units have none | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Plan & form

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **16–20-sided round plan** | 26% more floor per panel than a square; half the wind drag; self-bracing | curved furniture walls; the 20-gon's dome margins are thin without ribs | **WINNER** | `form_check.py` |
| Clusters of domes around courtyards (a 5k ft² 'mansion') | big homes from proven small spans; grow one dome at a time (Elemental) | more wall per floor; links and gutters between domes | adopt | `houses/compound_5k.json, house_designer.py` |
| Square or box plan | familiar furniture and codes | corner suction zones; Cd 1.2–1.4; needs bracing | fallback | `form_check.py` |
| One huge single span | open plan | the 24-gon hall passes at GSF 2.2 but big spans eat margin fast | niche | `houses/hall24.json` |
| Owners extend a closed dome ad hoc | freedom | Iquique's fires and flimsy add-ons | ~~killed~~ | `SYNTHESIS.md §3` |

## Roof

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ribbed dome: post-tensioned 16 in ribs + 6 in graded webs** | 35% less clay; rib GSF 4.2 (16-gon), 2.9 (20-gon); passes wind, snow, quake | stainless tendons to buy and re-check; a central mast to build it | **WINNER** | `dome_ribbed.py, making-system/KIT_OF_PARTS.md` |
| **Cocciopesto skin under overlapping fired scale tiles** | Roman 2,000-year record; its weight is what makes the dome pass wind | limewash every 1–3 years | **WINNER** | `SYNTHESIS.md` |
| Seat-step voussoirs + closing keys, course by course | builds without formwork or mortar; only compression on the clay | slow hand-setting; a cord guide per unit | adopt | `making-system/KIT_OF_PARTS.md` |
| Solid 16 in cellular voussoir dome to 51.8° | all compression; one die; GSF 1.62 in wind (16-gon) | heavier; 20-gon margins only 1.29–1.31 | fallback | `dome_check.py, dome_thrust.py` |
| 12 in dome voussoirs | less clay | no thrust line fits in 50 m/s wind; joints slide | ~~killed~~ | `dome_thrust.py` |
| Plain (unstressed) dry ribs | no steel | GSF ~1.2 in wind; joints slide | ~~killed~~ | `dome_ribbed.py` |
| Full hemisphere | taller room | hoop tension beyond 51.8° cracks the meridians (Pantheon, St Peter's) | ~~killed~~ | `making-system/KIT_OF_PARTS.md` |

## Envelope

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hung, interlocking fired siding over a vented cavity | ~60% less solar gain; each board lifts out; lock uses only 2–5% of strength | battens and hangers to buy; more parts | adopt | `cladding_check.py, making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Fluted drainage bricks on a crowned compacted-earth pad | moves roof water to a cistern and away from walls (Machu Picchu logic) | pad compaction and PI testing on site | adopt | `drainage_check.py` |
| Silicate mineral paint; light engobed tiles | vapour-open, UV-stable; reflectance 0.5 cut cooling ~30% | colour choices limited | adopt | `making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Siloxane repellent on the plinth only | ≥0.98 perm; ~10+ years | never on siding, dome or interiors | niche | `making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Lime textile-reinforced mortar | +100–536% in-plane strength; reversible, breathable | a repair, not a default | niche | `making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Siding hung on nibs alone | simplest | BS 5534 won't accept nibs against wind suction | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| A 'hydrophobic' fired face as the rain barrier | one fewer layer | fired ceramic is hydrophilic; beading needs siloxane that lasts 10–15 years | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Spray coatings (carbon-fibre epoxy, polyurea, elastomerics) | modern, fast | trap vapour and salts; hide cracks; 7–20 year recoats; none pass ICC 500 on masonry | ~~killed~~ | `making-system/ENVELOPE.md` |
| Earth tubes, evaporative cooling or night flushing in Arkansas | passive cooling | humid air: mould in tubes; evaporative cooling collapses at 80–90% RH | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Storm shelter

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Round drum + cap under 30°** | no corners; peak suction 9.4 kPa; roof takes only the 67 mph missile; dome coefficients exist | 44 kN uplift to tie down | **WINNER** | `shelter_check.py, business/SHELTER_PLAN.md` |
| Sacrificial fired skin + cavity + grouted cellular core | copies walls that already passed 100 mph | grout cure; needs lab testing ($75–175k) | test | `business/SHELTER_PLAN.md` |
| Box with flat roof | standard product | 21.8 kPa corner suction; 64 kN tie-down | fallback | `shelter_check.py` |
| Pyramid or steep cone that 'deflects' debris | looks strong | ICC 500 fires the missile perpendicular; faces ≥30° take the full 100 mph; no ASCE 7 coefficients | ~~killed~~ | `shelter_check.py` |
| Dry-stacked or sand-filled clay alone as a shelter wall | cheapest | 4 in solid brick shattered at ~76 mph | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Living materials

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hemp-lime or husk-lime blocks for interior walls | MBV 2–3.3; carbon store; quiet; code-listed as infill (IRC BL) | 0.15–0.4 MPa (non-load-bearing); 6–10 weeks to dry | adopt | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md, data/biolime.json, house_designer.py` |
| Hemp shiv briquettes as kiln fuel | ~18 MJ/kg, 2–4% ash vs husk's 15–20% | needs a supply | adopt | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Bio-lime infill in outer walls behind the siding | ~80% less wall clay; U ≈ 0.25–0.35 | not for the shelter core; weather and missile untested | test | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Hemp cover crop on worked-out pit benches | builds soil; ~13 t/ha reported on mine soil | dislikes wet compacted acid clay; licence needed | test | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Treated whole bamboo: roof framing, posts, verandahs under cover | 25 years treated, 100+ kept dry (minka, guadua) | borates are reproductive toxins; must stay covered and replaceable | test | `rock/BAMBOO_PROCESS.md` |
| Feed bamboo at death, mineralize inside, plasma + silicate 'ionized dip' | lab: silica + silane cut absorption 84.5%, MOE +15% | frontier on whole culms; toughness rarely measured | test | `rock/BAMBOO_PROCESS.md` |
| Mycelium interior acoustic panels | light; λ 0.03–0.05 | weak, absorbs water, combustible | niche | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Hempcrete cast in the shell | well-known | cast-in, not removable; a second wall system | ~~killed~~ | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Bamboo in place of steel rods or tendons | grown, cheap | ~1/13 the stiffness of steel; creeps; can't hold prestress | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Ceramized bamboo (SiC) or silicon-fed living bamboo | sounds permanent | SiC needs >1,400 °C and is brittle; no evidence Si feeding helps | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Mycelium or bacteria for self-healing structure | self-repair | no mortar joints to heal; puts organisms and water in dry walls | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Energy, kiln & sourcing

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fibre-lined kiln fired by a husk gasifier** | near-free fuel; ~80% less soot than old kilns; flue heat dries ware | firing control to learn | **WINNER** | `SYNTHESIS.md` |
| Separate husk-ash burner at 600–700 °C | makes reactive ash (the pozzolan) instead of cristobalite; waste heat to the dryer | XRD testing every batch; a silica dust hazard | adopt | `rock/BIO_MATERIALS.md` |
| Solar + battery runs the build, then the homes | renewable; outlives the build | capital; battery kept cool | adopt | `SYNTHESIS.md` |
| Wilcox pit sand + grog from kiln rejects + Jones Mill quarry sand | local, permitted, cheap | haul distance for quarry sand | adopt | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| 'The fired wall powers the house' | — | firing energy is spent as heat; a wall stores nothing recoverable | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| River sand-bar harvesting on the Ouachita | a self-refilling sand supply | ~98% of the watershed is dammed; downstream bed incision; 404/401/ESA permits | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |

## Business & scale

| idea | pros | cons | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A factory where clay meets rice husks (Malvern), shipping kits by truckload** | costs mostly fixed; price scales with tonnes and trucks; lean shells ~$20–25/ft² | real costs and scrap unknown until a pilot runs | **WINNER** | `business/BUSINESS_CASE.md, business_model.py` |
| **Storm shelter as the first certified product** | one clear standard; public funding; plays to heavy clay | $75–175k and 12–18 months to certify | **WINNER** | `business/SHELTER_PLAN.md` |
| Start tiny, grow on grants (NSF SBIR, EPA, USDA) | capital-light; each stage proves the next | grant timing; don't build the plan on one grant | adopt | `business/BUSINESS_CASE.md, business/NSF_SBIR_PROJECT_PITCH.md` |
| Own daylight robotics (gantry stacking, pre-assembly) | labour from 11.8 to 1.9 h/t; runs on solar hours | $125–420k; pays back only at volume | test | `production_line.py` |
| Open-method charity instead of a company (early view) | no moat needed | superseded once the factory-and-kit model gave a real price edge | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md (Overturned)` |
| Arkansas residential safe-room rebates as first funding | would pay buyers directly | Arkansas's program ended in 2016; FEMA money there goes to community safe rooms | ~~killed~~ | `GRAVEYARD.md` |
| Build 50 machines before one finished house | — | Open Source Ecology's scope creep | ~~killed~~ | `SYNTHESIS.md §3` |
